<result>## Report — bar_stool (primitive:cube:11)

**Result:** 53 authored (named) faces, 106 triangles, `unnamed: 0`, `0 intersecting · 0 unreachable`. Saved (`ok:true`).

**Bounding box:** x[-0.19, 0.19] m · y[0, 0.75] m · z[-0.19, 0.19] m — grounded at y=0, seat top at 0.75 m, footprint 0.38×0.38 m.

**Regions authored:**
- `seatTop` / `bottom`(consumed) / `right` / `left` / `back` / `front` — the seat slab (0.38 × 0.05 × 0.38 m), y=[0.70, 0.75]
- `legBackRight`, `legFrontRight`, `legBackLeft`, `legFrontLeft` (each `.cap` + `.wall`) — four legs, each with a short 0.19→0.04 m tapered flange at the slab (y=0.67–0.70) then a straight 0.04×0.04 m post down to y=0
- `stretcherRight.wall`, `stretcherLeft.wall` — footrest stretchers at y=[0.235, 0.265] (centered ~0.25 m), bridging front-to-back legs on each side

**Method:** Scaled the bootstrap cube into the slab, `basic-cut` the underside into a 2×2 grid, extruded each corner quad down in two stages (short taper + long straight run, scaling the intermediate cap to leg width so the taper doesn't drag the slab's own side faces — first attempt scaled the corner face *before* extruding and warped `right`/`back`, caught it via bbox and undid it). Stretchers: cut both facing leg walls at y=0.235/0.265 to isolate a matching band on *each* leg first, then extruded one band across the gap, used `select-audit unreachable` to grab the coincident mating faces on both sides in one shot and deleted them together — this reliably produced a clean welded junction (top/bottom edges manifold with faces:2) each time, versus doing the cuts after the extrude, which corrupted geometry once (stray vertices, a non-manifold edge) and had to be undone and redone in the corrected order. Splay: moved each leg's foot cap outward 0.025 m (only the segment below the stretcher ring bends, giving a natural kicked-out stance) rather than rotating, to keep the math exact and axis-aligned.

**Refusal hit:** `semantic-status` refused — `"the UV/paint focus bridge belongs to the visible ModelView; semantic-status cannot target a background model"` — this lane is a background tab (active model was `primitive:cube:3`). Per the skill's documented background-refusal families this is expected; `save` itself returned `ok:true`, which is save's own postcondition for successful semantic persistence (it re-reads the written blob and rolls back on a semantic drop), so I did not fight the refusal — I'm reporting it rather than force-switching tabs. A live-model `semantic-status`/cold-reopen check would need to be run from the visible session.

Claim dismissed at the end of the engagement.</result>
